questions.question: A pull-request bot sends the diff to Claude and posts findings. A PR contains a 4,000-line generated lockfile change. What is the best handling?
options: Split the lockfile into the system prompt
Reject all large PRs automatically
Send everything and hope
Exclude generated and lock files from the diff sent for review and review only meaningful source changes
questions.explanation: Filtering noise (lockfiles, generated code, binaries) reduces cost and improves review quality. Auto-rejecting is heavy-handed.

questions.question: A batch request in a submitted batch fails validation for one item. What happens to the others?
options: Remaining requests are processed twice
All requests are silently dropped
Each request is processed independently; one failing does not fail the rest, and the failure appears as an errored result
The entire batch is rejected
questions.explanation: Batch requests are independent, and per-request outcomes are reported individually. Check each result type and resubmit only the failures.

questions.question: A legal-research assistant needs to analyse very long contracts in one pass and also keep cost reasonable. Which consideration is most relevant when selecting the model?
options: The model's context window and long-context quality, balanced against per-token price and whether prompt caching can reduce repeated input cost
Only the model's name, because larger names always mean larger windows
Only output speed, since context length never affects cost
The number of letters in the model identifier
questions.explanation: Long documents require sufficient context capacity, and cost scales with tokens, so teams weigh window size, accuracy on long inputs and caching opportunities. The model name alone says nothing reliable.

questions.question: A team moves from the first-party Anthropic API to Google Vertex AI and finds that a newly released beta feature is unavailable there. What is the sound engineering response?
options: Rename the beta header to bypass the restriction
Wrap the call in a retry loop until it works
Check the platform's feature-availability documentation and design with a fallback, since third-party platforms can lag on beta features
Assume feature parity and ship
questions.explanation: Third-party platforms may differ in model IDs, auth, and available beta features. Verify support in the docs rather than assuming parity or retrying.

questions.question: A team wants Claude to refuse to guess when information is missing in a data-extraction task. They are debating whether lowering randomness will fix hallucinated values. What is the best guidance?
options: Hallucinations occur only when streaming is enabled, so switch to non-streaming
Lowering randomness makes output more consistent but not more truthful; instruct the model to return null for missing fields and validate the output against source text
Setting randomness to its minimum removes hallucination entirely
Adding more output tokens gives the model room to double-check itself automatically
questions.explanation: Reducing randomness changes how tokens are sampled, not whether the model's knowledge or the prompt supports the answer. Explicit instructions (allow null / unknown), schema validation and grounding checks address fabricated values.

questions.question: A client receives HTTP 529 overloaded_error from the Claude API during a traffic spike. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Fix the request body, since 529 means malformed input.
Retry immediately in a tight loop until it works.
Treat it as transient: retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and consider a fallback or queueing for non-urgent work.
Treat it as a permanent failure and rotate the API key.
questions.explanation: 529 indicates temporary API overload, a retriable condition best handled with backoff and jitter. Key rotation is for 401, request edits are for 400 errors, and tight retry loops worsen load.

questions.question: A content team generates marketing copy. A first model drafts it, and a second model scores it against a rubric and gives concrete feedback. The draft is regenerated until it meets the rubric or a retry limit is reached. Which pattern is this?
options: Evaluator-optimizer
Parallelization with sectioning
Orchestrator-workers
Routing
questions.explanation: Evaluator-optimizer pairs a generator with an evaluator in a feedback loop. It works best when there are clear evaluation criteria and iteration measurably improves the output.

questions.question: A Claude-driven service writes tool-call arguments to a database. Which practice protects against malformed or malicious values?
options: Interpolate values directly into SQL
Validate arguments against a schema and use parameterized queries
Trust the model because it is aligned
Disable logging
questions.explanation: Model-produced values are untrusted input; validate and parameterize to avoid injection.

questions.question: Select TWO. A team wants to give Claude Code a recurring, multi-step data-cleanup procedure that includes a validation script. Which are sound reasons to implement it as a Skill rather than a long CLAUDE.md section?
options: CLAUDE.md content is never loaded into context
Skills are the only way to run scripts in Claude Code
Instructions, reference files and scripts can be packaged together as one reusable unit
The body and bundled script load only when the task is relevant, saving context in other sessions
Skills execute on every tool call automatically without any model decision
questions.explanation: Skills offer progressive disclosure and bundle instructions with scripts and resources. They are model-selected, not automatic on every tool call (that is hooks), and CLAUDE.md is loaded at session start.

questions.question: A prompt for code review says 'Find all bugs.' The model returns many style nitpicks and misses a race condition. Which refinement is best?
options: Remove the 'Find all bugs' line.
Define what counts as a bug for this review (correctness, concurrency, security), ask for severity and evidence, and explicitly exclude style issues.
Tell the model it will be penalised for missing anything.
Ask for as many comments as possible.
questions.explanation: Scoping the task and defining output expectations focuses attention on the target issues. Maximising comments adds noise, removing the line removes the task, and threats are unreliable.

questions.question: A mobile app team wants to call Claude directly from the app with an embedded API key to reduce latency. What is the best recommendation?
options: Route requests through a backend that holds the key, authenticates users and applies rate limits
Ship a separate key per app version and never rotate
Put the key in an app-readable config file
Obfuscate the key inside the app binary
questions.explanation: Any key shipped to a client can be extracted. A backend proxy keeps the key secret and lets you enforce authn, authz and quotas.

questions.question: A Python team is calling Claude from a backend service. A junior developer proposes hand-writing HTTP requests with the requests library to avoid 'extra dependencies'. What is the main advantage of using the official Anthropic SDK instead?
options: The SDK stores conversation history on Anthropic's servers automatically
The SDK bypasses rate limits because it authenticates differently
The SDK wraps the REST API with typed request/response objects, automatic retries with backoff, timeout handling, streaming helpers and header management
The SDK uses a different, faster network protocol than the REST API
questions.explanation: Official SDKs are thin wrappers over the same REST API, adding typing, retries, streaming helpers and consistent error classes. They do not use a different protocol, circumvent rate limits or keep server-side conversation state.

questions.question: Where is the best place to configure a hook that blocks writes to `.env` files for everyone working in a repository?
options: The system prompt of one session
A developer's personal `~/.claude/settings.json` only
The project's `.claude/settings.json`, committed to version control
A comment inside CLAUDE.md
questions.explanation: Project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` is shared through the repo so the whole team gets the same hook. User-level settings affect only one person, and CLAUDE.md is guidance, not enforcement.

questions.question: Which TWO changes make a CI-integrated Claude code review more trustworthy? Select TWO.
options: Hide its token usage
Provide the diff plus relevant surrounding context and project conventions
Allow it to push fixes to main
Run it with no repository context
Require findings to cite file and line that a script verifies exist in the diff
questions.explanation: Context improves relevance, and programmatic verification of citations catches hallucinated findings.

questions.question: A travel-planning assistant is started fresh each day, but users expect it to remember stated dietary restrictions. Which design best fits?
options: Persist a small, user-scoped memory of stable preferences and inject it at session start, letting the user view and correct it.
Store preferences in the system prompt of all users.
Rely on the model's weights to remember each user.
Replay the complete history of all past sessions at every start.
questions.explanation: Small, curated, user-scoped memory delivers continuity without bloat or leakage and allows correction. Replaying everything bloats, models do not retain per-user data between calls, and a global prompt leaks and mismatches users.

questions.question: Which TWO are examples of least privilege for an LLM agent that triages support tickets? Select TWO.
options: Access to the entire company file share in case it is useful
Giving the model the database root password so it can fix issues itself
A single API key with account-wide admin scope
Credentials scoped to the support queue and expiring after the task
Tools limited to reading tickets and drafting replies, with sending requiring human approval
questions.explanation: Least privilege means only the capabilities and scopes the task requires, ideally short-lived. Broad or admin credentials give an injected agent excess power.

questions.question: A team is shown a request with one example question/answer pair followed by the real question. Which term describes this prompting technique?
options: Single-shot (one-shot) prompting
Zero-shot prompting
Chain-of-thought fine-tuning
Prompt caching
questions.explanation: Zero-shot gives no examples, single-shot gives exactly one, and multi-shot (few-shot) gives several. Providing examples in the prompt is in-context learning and does not modify the model.

questions.question: You enable manual extended thinking (`thinking: {type: "enabled"}`) and also set tool_choice to force a specific tool. What should you expect?
options: Forcing a tool (any or tool) is not supported with extended thinking; only auto or none are allowed
Everything works and thinking improves accuracy
Thinking is silently disabled
The tool is called twice
questions.explanation: With manual extended thinking only tool_choice `auto` or `none` is supported; `any` or `tool` returns an error. If you need a forced tool call, turn thinking off for that request, or use `auto` with a prompt instruction.

questions.question: Stakeholders say the assistant 'should never be wrong about refund policy.' What requirement refinement is most realistic?
options: Guarantee 100% accuracy through prompting
Ground answers in the authoritative policy document, define escalation to a human when uncertain, and set measurable accuracy targets
Remove the human agents
Disable the policy lookup
questions.explanation: LLM systems cannot promise zero error; requirements should specify grounding, escalation, and tested accuracy.

questions.question: A team needs Claude to follow a 12-step code-review checklist with company-specific conventions, but the workflow involves no external system access beyond reading files. What is the lightest-weight reusable option?
options: A Skill containing the checklist and conventions (optionally with reference files)
A new MCP server with a `review` tool
Fine-tuning a model
A custom tool that hits a remote API
questions.explanation: When no external system is needed, a Skill packages instructions and resources with low context overhead. An MCP server adds infrastructure that is not warranted.

questions.question: A POST /summaries endpoint calls Claude and charges tokens. A mobile client retries on flaky networks and sometimes produces two charges. Which fix is best?
options: Switch the endpoint to GET
Disable retries on the client
Cache all responses for 24 hours regardless of input
Accept an Idempotency-Key header and return the stored result for repeated keys
questions.explanation: An idempotency key lets the server dedupe retried POSTs without disabling retries. GET is semantically wrong for side effects, and blind caching returns wrong results.

questions.question: A multi-agent research system spends far more tokens than a single-agent chat for the same question. A stakeholder asks when that cost is justified. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Always, because more agents always improve answer quality
When the task is high-value and breadth-heavy or parallelizable enough that the extra tokens buy meaningfully better results
Never, because multi-agent systems cannot beat a single agent
Only when each agent uses the same prompt, to keep behavior consistent
questions.explanation: Multi-agent setups multiply token use, so they pay off for valuable, wide or parallelizable tasks. Tasks that need tightly shared context or few independent threads often fit a single agent better.

questions.question: A research agent calls a web-search tool that returns full page text (about 8,000 tokens per hit). It needs only a few facts from each page, and long sessions exhaust the context. Which design best manages this?
options: Reduce the number of searches to one per session regardless of the question.
Always append the full page text so no information is lost.
Store all pages in the system prompt so they are cached.
Delegate each page read to a subagent or extraction step that returns only the relevant facts to the main agent.
questions.explanation: Isolating noisy reads in a separate context and returning distilled results keeps the orchestrator's context lean. Appending everything causes bloat, limiting searches harms quality, and stuffing pages in the system prompt does not reduce tokens or relevance problems.

questions.question: A product team wants Claude to answer in a fixed support-reply template. They need the model to fill in only the variable parts. Which approach is most dependable?
options: Provide the template in a language other than the user's.
Request a creative answer inspired by the template.
Give no template and post-process in code.
Describe the template with named placeholders in tags, show a filled example, and instruct the model to output only the filled template.
questions.explanation: A clear template with placeholders and an example constrains the response structure. The other options either confuse the format or push all work onto brittle post-processing.

questions.question: A team's Claude Code usage shows rising cost: each session loads a very large CLAUDE.md plus many rarely-used skills. Which design change is best aligned with context hygiene?
options: Trim CLAUDE.md to essentials and move situational guidance into path-scoped rules or on-demand skills
Disable the context window limit
Add more content to CLAUDE.md so Claude needs fewer questions
Rename CLAUDE.md to lowercase
questions.explanation: Always-loaded instructions consume context every session; situational content is better loaded on demand via path-scoped rules or skills. Neither adding content nor renaming helps.

questions.question: A repo already has a maintained AGENTS.md for other coding agents. The team now adds a CLAUDE.md with Claude-specific notes and finds Claude Code no longer reads AGENTS.md on its own. What is the best way to reuse its content?
options: Rename AGENTS.md to settings.json
Import it from CLAUDE.md with an @AGENTS.md line so both are loaded
Copy AGENTS.md content into every prompt
Delete CLAUDE.md
questions.explanation: When a CLAUDE.md exists, Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md files and not AGENTS.md by default; an @ import pulls the shared content in, keeping one source of truth.

questions.question: An engineer's PreToolUse safety hook throws an unhandled exception for certain inputs. In the Agent SDK's default behavior, the tool call may proceed to the normal permission flow. Which configuration makes the guard fail closed?
options: Increase the callback's temperature setting
Register the hook under the Notification event instead
Set the matcher's failure behavior to block (for example onFailure: "block") so a failing callback blocks the action
Return an empty object from the callback after catching all errors
questions.explanation: By default, a failing callback does not necessarily block the action. Setting onFailure to block makes a crashing guard stop the tool call. Catching errors and returning an empty object would silently allow it.

questions.question: A 429 appears even though the app sends few requests, but each request has a very large prompt. Which TWO statements are accurate and useful? Select TWO.
options: Disabling streaming raises the token limit
Raising max_tokens increases the available output-token quota
Limits are measured in input and output tokens per minute as well as requests per minute, so the token limit is likely being hit
Rate limits only count requests, so this cannot be a rate limit
Caching the repeated prefix helps, because on most models cache_read_input_tokens do not count toward ITPM
questions.explanation: Rate limits cover RPM, ITPM and OTPM, so large prompts can exhaust the token limit first. For most models only uncached input (input_tokens plus cache_creation_input_tokens) counts toward ITPM, so prompt caching increases effective throughput. max_tokens does not factor into OTPM limits.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the relationship between the Claude SDKs and the REST API are correct? Select TWO.
options: SDK usage changes the model's pricing
The REST API can only be called through an SDK
The SDKs are wrappers that send the same HTTP requests you could send yourself
New API features are sometimes available via raw HTTP or beta SDK namespaces before they reach a stable SDK surface
The SDKs use a proprietary binary protocol that the REST API cannot imitate
questions.explanation: SDKs are convenience layers over the public REST API; beta features may require beta headers or beta namespaces. They do not change protocol, access or price.

questions.question: An agent loop runs a research task that can proceed down many paths. The team wants the model, not the code, to decide the order and number of tool calls, with a clear stop when the question is answered. Which is the best loop termination design?
options: Stop after exactly one tool call
Continue while the model requests tools; stop when it returns a final response or when a safety limit such as max iterations or budget is hit
Stop when the output exceeds 10 characters
Stop only when the user closes the browser
questions.explanation: A model-driven loop ends on a natural final response, with limits as a backstop. Fixed counts fit workflows rather than agents.

questions.question: A team wants Claude to return both a short explanation for humans and structured data for code. Which design is most robust?
options: Ask for the explanation and data interleaved in a single paragraph.
Return prose and regex out the numbers.
Use a schema with separate fields (for example 'summary' and 'data') so the code reads only the structured fields.
Use two different models and compare the outputs.
questions.explanation: Separating human-readable and machine-readable parts in distinct schema fields keeps parsing deterministic. Regex over prose and interleaving are brittle.

questions.question: Which TWO describe good practice for the final report returned by a subagent to its lead agent? Select TWO.
options: Return only 'done' to minimize tokens
Return unstructured stream-of-consciousness reasoning
Return the full raw transcript of every tool call for completeness
Return a concise distilled result with the key findings and sources the lead needs
Follow an output format that the lead agent specified in the delegation prompt
questions.explanation: Subagents exist to protect the lead's context, so reports should be dense and structured. Raw transcripts defeat isolation, and 'done' loses the findings.

questions.question: An application sends a tool_result for a tool_use_id Claude never produced. What is the likely outcome?
options: The API rewrites the id automatically
The API returns a validation error because every tool_result must correspond to a tool_use block from the previous assistant turn
The result is queued for a later turn
Claude silently treats it as extra context
questions.explanation: tool_result blocks must reference a tool_use from the preceding assistant message; mismatched ids produce a 400-style error. This is a common bug in harnesses that reuse or fabricate ids.

questions.question: Which requirement most strongly points toward a custom tool or MCP server rather than a Skill?
options: Claude must call a live external API with authentication and get current data
Claude needs written guidance on tone and formatting
Claude should know team naming conventions
Claude should follow a documented review process
questions.explanation: Skills carry instructions (and optional scripts/resources), but live external system access with credentials is what tools and MCP servers provide. The other items are knowledge and procedure.

questions.question: Which TWO are benefits of infrastructure as code for deploying a Claude-backed service? Select TWO.
options: Elimination of all outages
Automatic prompt improvement
Reproducible environments
Free API usage
Reviewable, versioned infrastructure changes
questions.explanation: IaC provides repeatability and code review for infra, but not guaranteed uptime or cost savings on API use.

questions.question: A product team wants the model's JSON answers rendered into a form. Occasionally the response stops mid-object. Which application behavior is most appropriate?
options: Check stop_reason; if it is max_tokens the output is truncated, so raise the limit or retry and never render the partial object as complete
Switch to a smaller model to avoid truncation
Render whatever arrived since JSON is forgiving
Always append a closing brace to fix it
questions.explanation: A stop_reason of max_tokens signals truncated output, which must be handled explicitly rather than patched or displayed as complete. A smaller model does not address the token limit.

questions.question: A developer adds cache_control but cache_read_input_tokens stays at zero on every call. The system prompt starts with 'Current time: <timestamp>'. Which TWO things should they investigate or fix? Select TWO.
options: Confirm the cached prefix meets the model's minimum cacheable length, since shorter prefixes are silently not cached
Set the model temperature to zero, which caching requires
Remove cache_control, because it can be used only once per account
Wait for the weekend, when cache hits are reported
Move volatile content such as the timestamp after the cached breakpoint, because the prefix changes every request
questions.explanation: Caching matches an exact prefix, so a timestamp near the top invalidates everything after it. Prompts below the model-specific minimum are processed without caching and without an error; check usage.cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens. Temperature is irrelevant, and cache_control can be used many times (up to four breakpoints per request).

questions.question: A developer has spent a Claude Code session debugging a payments bug and now wants to start work on an unrelated CSS refactor in the same repository. Which action best supports session hygiene?
options: Keep the same session so Claude remembers everything, since more context always improves results
Ask Claude to forget the payments bug in a normal message
Run /compact after every message regardless of the task
Run /clear (or start a fresh session) before the unrelated task so stale debugging context does not occupy the window or bias the work
questions.explanation: Unrelated tasks should start with a clean context; /clear resets it cheaply. Leftover context consumes the window and can distract. Compacting after every message is wasteful, and asking Claude to 'forget' does not remove tokens from the context.

questions.question: A support platform wants specialist agents (billing, tech, shipping) that hand a conversation to one another as the topic changes, with no central controller deciding each step. Which pattern does this resemble?
options: A prompt chain with fixed steps
An evaluator-optimizer loop
A swarm of peer agents that hand off to each other
A parallelization pattern using voting
questions.explanation: Peer-to-peer handoffs without a central controller describe a swarm; a supervisor hierarchy would instead centralize routing.

questions.question: A team wants shared permission rules and hooks to be committed to the repo, while an individual developer keeps experimental, uncommitted overrides. Which pair of files fits?
options: `~/.claude/settings.json` for shared and `CLAUDE.md` for personal
`.claude/settings.json` for shared and `.claude/settings.local.json` for personal
Managed settings for shared and user settings for personal
`.claude/settings.local.json` for shared and `.claude/settings.json` for personal
questions.explanation: The project settings file is meant to be checked in, while settings.local.json is gitignored for personal overrides.

questions.question: A product manager asks whether Claude Code and the raw API should be expected to follow a repo's coding standards in the same way. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Neither can follow coding standards
Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files as context automatically, whereas an API app has no such mechanism unless it supplies the standards in its own prompt
The API reads CLAUDE.md but Claude Code does not
Both automatically read the repository's CLAUDE.md
questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md loading is a Claude Code feature; a raw API integration only sees what the application sends. Teams must carry standards into API prompts explicitly.

questions.question: An incident occurs when a prompt update causes malformed outputs. What is the best response process?
options: Blame the model
Delete logs
Roll back to the previous version, then conduct a blameless post-mortem and add a regression test
Hot-edit the prompt repeatedly in production
questions.explanation: Fast rollback restores service; post-mortems and tests prevent recurrence.

questions.question: A new MCP server written with FastMCP needs to expose a customer profile at URIs like `customers://{customer_id}/profile`. Which construct fits?
options: A resource template registered with @mcp.resource using a URI containing a parameter
A prompt decorated with @mcp.prompt
A hard-coded list of one resource per customer
A tool that must always be called first
questions.explanation: FastMCP supports parameterised URI templates on @mcp.resource so a single handler serves many entities. Prompts are templates for user messages and static per-customer registration does not scale.

questions.question: A developer passes a model-generated tool input directly into a REST call to an internal service without parsing the JSON or validating the schema. What principle does this violate?
options: Validation should happen only on the model's thinking blocks
Schemas are only needed for streaming responses
Model output is always valid JSON, so validation is wasted effort
Treat model output as untrusted data: parse it defensively, validate against a schema, and handle malformed or unexpected values before using it
questions.explanation: Even well-behaved models can produce malformed or unexpected output, so integrations should parse and validate before acting on it. This is basic engineering hygiene for any untrusted input.

questions.question: A tool-using agent reads a GitHub issue from a public repo and, following text in the issue, calls a tool that reads a private repo and posts its contents as a public comment. Which principle was most clearly violated?
options: Using too low a token limit
Separation of untrusted content from the agent's privileged tools and data (the 'lethal trifecta' of private data, untrusted content, and external communication)
Using a non-streaming API
Missing prompt caching
questions.explanation: The combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and an exfiltration channel is the dangerous pattern. Break at least one leg, e.g., scope tokens per repo or disable external posting.

questions.question: A team needs a hard guarantee that an agent can never delete production data, regardless of what the model decides. Which TWO implementations are most reliable? Select TWO.
options: Lowering temperature to 0 so the model is consistent
Running the agent with credentials and sandbox access that simply lack delete rights on production data
A PreToolUse hook that inspects the tool call and returns a deny decision for destructive commands, in code outside the model
Asking the model to double check each command before running it
Adding 'never delete production data' in capital letters to the system prompt
questions.explanation: Deterministic code at tool-call time and least-privilege credentials are enforced outside the model. Prompt instructions and low temperature reduce the likelihood of a bad call but give no guarantee.

questions.question: An app shows streamed answers in a browser and also calls tools. Which TWO behaviors make for a robust streaming UX? Select TWO.
options: Handle stream errors or interruptions by letting the user retry without losing prior content
Wait for the whole response before showing anything to simulate reliability
Execute tool calls as soon as the first partial JSON fragment appears
Display text deltas as they arrive and show a status when a tool call is in progress
Hide stop_reason from the client logic
questions.explanation: Good streaming UX renders incremental text, indicates tool activity and recovers from interruptions. Tool inputs must be complete before execution, and waiting for the full response defeats streaming.

questions.question: The team's committed .claude/settings.json sets "model" to a Sonnet model. One developer wants to use Opus in this project without changing teammates' behavior or committing anything. What is the best approach?
options: Set the model in .claude/settings.local.json, which has higher precedence than the shared project file and stays personal
Rename the project folder
Edit the committed .claude/settings.json and push
Change the ~/.claude/settings.json file, which outranks project settings
questions.explanation: Project local settings sit above shared project settings in precedence and are for personal overrides. User settings rank below the project file, so they would not win.

questions.question: A backend engineer sees that the SDK is configured with its default retry behavior and asks what it does. Which statement is accurate?
options: The SDK retries every error including 401 and 400 until success
The SDK never retries; every failure must be retried by the application
The SDK retries only when streaming is enabled
The SDK automatically retries a small number of times on connection errors and retryable statuses such as 408, 409, 429 and 5xx, with backoff, and you can configure or disable this
questions.explanation: Official SDKs include default retry logic for transient failures with exponential backoff and expose options to change the count. Client errors like 400 and 401 are not retried because retrying cannot fix them.

questions.question: A team notes that caches written by the default setting seem to disappear when traffic is sparse overnight. Which feature of caching explains this, and what is a reasonable mitigation?
options: Cache entries expire after a time-to-live (five minutes by default, refreshed on each hit); for infrequent traffic consider the longer one-hour TTL option or accept misses
Caches never expire but are evicted randomly when the account is idle
Caches expire only at midnight UTC
Caches are deleted whenever a new deployment happens
questions.explanation: Default cache entries last about five minutes and are refreshed on use, so sparse traffic misses. A longer TTL option exists at a higher write cost, which should be weighed against hit rates.

questions.question: An API returns a structured response whose 'confidence' field is generated by the model itself and equals 0.97. The team plans to auto-approve loans above 0.9. What is the key concern?
options: The threshold should be exactly 0.99.
Model-reported confidence is not a calibrated probability; decisions need independent validation, thresholds tested against labelled data, and human review for high-stakes cases.
The value should have been 97 rather than 0.97.
Confidence fields are not allowed in JSON.
questions.explanation: Self-reported scores are not reliable calibration; they must be validated against ground truth, and high-stakes decisions need oversight. The format of the number is irrelevant.

questions.question: With a self-hosted sandbox in Managed Agents, what runs on the customer's infrastructure?
options: The model weights and inference
The entire agent loop, including model sampling
An environment worker that claims work items and executes the agent's tool calls locally, posting results back
Only the web interface for viewing session transcripts
questions.explanation: Anthropic keeps running the agent loop and model; the worker you operate runs tools such as bash and file operations in your environment.

questions.question: Your service gets HTTP 400 invalid_request_error: a field name is misspelled in the request. What should the retry policy do?
options: Retry with a larger max_tokens.
Do not retry unchanged; log the error and fix the request, since 4xx client errors will keep failing.
Retry five times with backoff.
Switch to another region and retry.
questions.explanation: A 400 is a terminal client error: identical retries fail identically. Backoff is for transient errors; region and max_tokens are unrelated.
